integrity: The proof reduces every condition to the two part sums and two positive-label sums. A universal weight-three lower bound is proved first. Explicit parity-sensitive constructions attain weight three for smaller part two or three. When both parts have size at least four, a side-sum-two construction gives weight four, while any hypothetical weight-three function forces a negative label on both sides and hence side sums at least two each, a contradiction. The published cycle result supplies only the K_{2,2} boundary.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to complete bipartite graphs with both parts of size at least two.
The K_{2,2}=C_4 boundary value is already covered by the published cycle formula and is not part of the originality claim.
Finite verification covers part sizes from two through twelve and is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed equivalent complete-bipartite result may exist.
title: Signed double Italian domination of complete bipartite graphs
